title: Private deployments: RBAC v2 policy bundle distribution + update mechanism (installer integration) and docs
creator: Hanae Suzuki
description:
Problem
Private deployments (VPC/on-prem, including air-gapped) need a reliable way to receive and update RBAC v2 policy bundles. In Hosted we can fetch policy bundles from a central service and invalidate caches; in Private we have to support:
- offline installs (no egress)
- upgrade-time and post-install updates
- verifiable authenticity (supply chain)
- version skew handling across control plane + console services
- predictable rollback behavior and auditability

This issue implements the distribution/update mechanism and integrates it into the Private installer + upgrade flow, with documentation for operators.

Goals
1) Define and implement a supported path to get policy bundles onto a Private cluster:
   - online: pull from Redwood artifact endpoint (or customer mirror)
   - offline: customer provides an artifact during install/upgrade
2) Ensure authenticity + integrity of bundles (signed artifacts) and document verification.
3) Provide versioning rules and compatibility checks (min/max supported schema + policy version).
4) Implement installer hooks that place the bundle where services can read it, trigger safe reload, and emit audit events.
5) Provide operator docs + runbook (how to update, how to roll back, what to monitor).

Non-goals
- Building a full policy authoring UI for Private.
- Supporting arbitrary policy evaluation engines in Private; we ship Redwood policy format.
- Deep identity provider refactors (SSO/SAML) beyond role mapping already tracked elsewhere.

Proposed approach (implementation notes)
Artifact format
- Ship a single signed bundle artifact: rbac-policy-bundle_<policy_version>_<schema_version>.tar.zst
- Contents:
  - policy.json (or policy.yaml if ADR chooses YAML; current assumption: JSON in artifact even if authoring YAML)
  - manifest.json (bundle_id, policy_version, schema_version, created_at, git_sha)
  - signature.sig + public key id (see signing section)

Signing + verification
- Bundle produced in rbac-policy-bundle CI and signed using Redwood release signing key.
- Private installer verifies signature before applying. Fail closed if signature invalid.
- Allow option to pin a specific public key id in installer config for regulated customers.

Placement + reload
- Installer writes verified bundle to a shared volume/config path (e.g., /etc/redwood/policy/bundles/current).
- Services mount read-only and watch for atomic symlink swap (current -> <bundle_id>).
- Services load policy on startup; reload on change with debounce.
- Authz library caches per-org policy; reload increments local policy cache epoch and emits metric.

Version skew + compatibility
- Each service declares:
  - supported_schema_versions: [min,max]
  - supported_policy_versions: >= X (optional)
- Installer checks compatibility against the currently deployed service versions:
  - If schema_version too new: block apply with clear error and operator guidance (“upgrade services first”).
  - If schema_version older: allow apply but warn if below recommended.
- Keep N previous bundles (default 3) on disk for rollback.

Update flows
- Install-time: allow passing bundle path (offline) OR enable auto-fetch (online).
- Upgrade-time: if auto-fetch enabled, installer pulls the recommended bundle matching the deployed release; otherwise uses operator-supplied.
- Post-install: provide `redwood-private policy apply --bundle <path|url>` command that:
  - verifies signature
  - stages bundle
  - swaps symlink atomically
  - records audit event: policy_bundle_applied (actor, source, bundle_id, policy_version, result)

Observability + audit
- Emit audit events on:
  - verification failure
  - apply success/failure
  - rollback
- Emit metrics:
  - policy_bundle_current_version{service}
  - policy_bundle_reload_total{service,result}
  - policy_bundle_verify_failure_total{reason}

Documentation deliverables
- Operator guide: “Updating RBAC policy bundles in Private (online/offline)”.
- Air-gapped guide: how to obtain artifacts, verify signatures, and apply during upgrades.
- Troubleshooting: interpreting errors (schema too new, signature invalid), rollback steps.

Acceptance criteria
- Private installer supports specifying a bundle artifact path and applies it during install.
- Private installer supports auto-fetch mode for connected installs (with configurable URL / mirror).
- Bundle signature is verified; invalid signature prevents apply.
- Services reload policy on atomic update without restart (control plane + console backend at minimum).
- Compatibility checks prevent applying unsupported schema versions.
- Audit events emitted for apply/rollback with enough context for customer audits.
- Docs published (internal + customer-facing where appropriate) and linked from Private deployment docs.

Links
- ADR: policy format + versioning semantics (Architecture/ADR-014)
- Policy bundle repo PR (initial): github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr_214
- Policy bundle packaging (Private): github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr_219
- Authz lib caching: github/redwood/pr_18477
- Audit log enrichment: github/redwood/pr_18522 / audit-log-exporter/pr_88

Test plan
- Unit tests: signature verification wrapper; manifest parsing; compatibility checks.
- Integration tests (kind/minikube): apply bundle -> services reload -> permission checks reflect new bundle.
- Offline test: installer apply from local artifact w/ no network.
- Rollback test: apply invalid bundle (blocked), apply older bundle (allowed w/ warning), rollback to previous bundle.

Rollout notes
- Feature flag: private.rbac_v2_policy_bundle_distribution
- Default to “install-time bundle required” for air-gapped template; “auto-fetch enabled” for connected template.
- Provide a migration note for existing Private customers upgrading from RBAC v1 -> v2 (ENG-5389).
comments: 2025-02-10 (Fatima Noor): Drafted artifact layout + atomic symlink swap approach. Key open question: do we want services to watch filesystem or use an internal admin endpoint to trigger reload? Leaning filesystem watch to avoid adding a sensitive endpoint in Private.

2025-02-14 (Jordan Lee): +1 filesystem watch. If we add an endpoint, it becomes another permissioned action and we need to thread it through the inventory + RBAC checks. Keep it simple: read-only mount + inotify watch, reload on symlink change.

2025-02-18 (Kevin Osei): Please ensure policy apply/rollback emits audit events with actor context. For air-gapped customers, the actor will often be a local operator account—still needs to appear in the audit log export pipeline. Add reason codes for signature failure vs schema incompatibility.

2025-02-21 (Hanae Suzuki): For regulated Private installs we need a way to pin signing key id (or rotate keys). Can we support a list of trusted key ids in installer config? Also confirm we keep last 3 bundles for rollback by default.

2025-02-26 (Connor O'Brien): Rollout concern: upgrades may deploy new services + old policy bundle. Installer should apply the release-recommended bundle as part of upgrade when auto-fetch enabled; otherwise warn loudly that bundle may be incompatible until operator updates.

2025-03-03 (Fatima Noor): Implemented installer `policy apply` command with verify->stage->swap. Added compatibility checks against declared supported schema versions read from service configmap. Pending review on where supported versions should live (service container labels vs configmap).

2025-03-07 (Sean Gallagher): Please add a guardrail for incident scenarios: if a bad bundle blocks SRE break-glass permissions in Private, rollback must be a single command and not require restarting pods. Include runbook section “If you are locked out”.

2025-03-12 (Elliot Price): Docs draft ready; needs final confirmation on artifact naming + exact CLI command flags. Also please include a short snippet for customers to verify signature offline (sha256 + signature check) with commands we actually ship.

2025-03-18 (Fatima Noor): Marking In Review. PRs up: rbac-policy-bundle packaging + private installer integration + docs. Remaining: add explicit audit event for rollback and finalize the ‘trusted key ids’ config option per Hanae’s ask.
